notes: MASTERPLAN SECTION 14 - THE CAMPAIGN'S MOST IMPORTANT PAST INCIDENT. At worker concurrency 3 this runtime failed 48 of 54 pages with tensor-shape errors, and the set of pages that succeeded changed between repeats, so no accuracy metric could be computed. The rule is absolute: concurrency per worker = 1, throughput scales by horizontal replicas only, never 1 worker x concurrency 8. adapter.py refuses to load with cfg.max_concurrency != 1 rather than clamping it, because a caller who asked for more has a wrong plan and silently correcting it hides the wrong plan. `vlm-engine` is a public backend name that MinerU resolves at call time with get_vlm_engine(inference_engine='auto'), which picks vllm-engine when vLLM is importable and transformers otherwise; the base image does ship vLLM, so the adapter reads the resolved engine and fails closed unless it equals inference_config.expected_vlm_engine. D59 (2026-09-04, after the real canary on pod plz5obsz7ega3a hit the FATAL this preflight is designed to raise): expected_vlm_engine was pinned to 'transformers', which is wrong for this image, not a MinerU bug - mineru/utils/engine_utils.py's _select_linux_engine always returns 'vllm' (formatted 'vllm-engine') when `import vllm` succeeds, and it does on vllm/vllm-openai:v0.21.0; the checkpoint's own official_inference_config (model_registry.json) already names backend 'vllm-engine'; and MinerU's own docker/global/Dockerfile FROMs this same vllm/vllm-openai base image, so auto-detecting vllm-engine on it is the path MinerU's own build documents, not an accident. expected_vlm_engine is now 'vllm-engine' and official_runtime is 'vllm' to match; adapter.py's ModelSingleton (mineru/backend/vlm/vlm_analyze.py) holds the vllm-engine model as an in-process vllm.LLM object, not an HTTP server, so this stays consistent with "does NOT start a model server" below. Resolution provenance and every open question live in provenance.json next to this file. D16/D34 (2026-09-03 second integration pass): model_repo / model_revision is the WEIGHTS repository (opendatalab/MinerU2.5-Pro-2605-1.2B @ bff20d4a, re-verified read-only against the Hugging Face revision API on 2026-09-03); runtime_repository / runtime_revision is the RUNTIME CODE repository (opendatalab/MinerU @ fbb1257a, re-verified against the GitHub commits API). prompt_kind is "none": the vlm-engine backend takes no prompt and adapter.py refuses a non-empty prompt_text. This runtime does NOT start a model server - MinerU runs in-process through do_parse - so entrypoint.sh keeps `exec` per D19. Framework-floor audit (2026-09-03, after the GLM-OCR canary died on an unrecognised model_type): the required framework floor, what the pinned base image actually ships, the action taken and the evidence URLs are recorded in provenance.json under framework_floor_audit. bootstrap.sh asserts the pinned framework versions and that the framework recognises this checkpoint's architecture before anything starts. D79 (2026-09-04, pod 8uzvgo0oj1vi43): MinerU's two parse paths do not agree on this image. do_parse resolves 'auto' to vllm-engine and returned the layout answer ']]<|><|><|><|>' with an empty body for every page, three canaries running; aio_do_parse resolves to vllm-async-engine and returned correct markdown for the same page in the same process from the adapter's own kwargs. Probes on pod x5kia8xy68w500 had already cleared the kwargs, the env and the calling thread. The vendor's `mineru` command is correct because since 3.4.4 it does not parse in its own process: it starts a LocalAPIServer, and that server is on the async path. adapter.py therefore calls aio_do_parse on an event loop it owns on its own thread (the engine binds to the loop it was created on, so a fresh asyncio.run per page would abandon the cached predictor), and expected_vlm_engine is now 'vllm-async-engine'. This runtime still does NOT start a model server: the async engine is an in-process AsyncLLMEngine, not an HTTP server.
